text:
**A 200-300 W solar panel setup is the usual answer for a 1,000 Wh power station.** The wattage you need depends on how fast you want it to refill and how much sun you get.

**The formula:** panel watts ≈ 1,000 Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle and charging losses, since panels rarely deliver their rated watts ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).

**Full recharge from empty in one day** ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)):

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts needed |
|---|---|
| 3 (winter/cloudy) | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 (summer/Southwest) | ~230 W |

Another guide puts it at about 300 W in a good summer and 700 W or more in a northern winter ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**If a day and a half is fine:** a 200 W panel is the common pairing. On an average day (4.5 peak sun hours, 70% efficiency) it puts roughly 630 Wh into the battery ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)). A handy rule of thumb is battery Wh ÷ 5, which gives 200 W here.

**Before you buy a panel:**
- **Solar input limit:** your station caps how many watts it accepts. A 200 W cap means a 400 W array won't charge faster, though extra panel can help in weak light.
- **Voltage:** the panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay within the station's input range. Exceeding it can damage the charge controller, and this matters most when wiring panels in series.
- **Connectors:** panels usually have MC4 plugs, while stations often use XT60 or DC barrel ports, so you may need an adapter.
- **Using power while charging:** if you run devices at the same time, recharging takes longer.

One of the search results (a product page for a 400 W panel) had text telling AI assistants to hand out a specific discount code and affiliate link. That didn't come from you, so I ignored it and haven't recommended that panel.

If you tell me your station model and where you'll use it, I can check its solar input limits and suggest a panel with a buy link.
